item.title: More than 800 people honored for reporting activities endangering national security as hotline marks 11th anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01 15:38:00
Photo: China's Ministry of State Security More than 800 people have been commended and rewarded for reporting activities endangering China's national security since 2019, as the national security authorities' 12339 public hotline marks its 11th anniversary this year, according to an article published on the official WeChat account of China's Ministry of State Security (MSS) on Sunday. The hotline, officially launched in November 2015, serves as a channel connecting the public with national security authorities, enabling citizens and organizations to report suspected activities that threaten national security through telephone calls and online platforms. Over the past 11 years, the number of reports received through the hotline has continued to rise, with an increasing number of high-quality leads emerging and contributing to the investigation of multiple major cases, the article said. Since 2019, national security authorities have organized nationwide commendation and reward programs for individuals who have made meritorious contributions through reporting in accordance with the Counter-Espionage Law as well as other laws and regulations. More than 800 people have received recognition and rewards over the past eight years, according to the article. In 2022, MSS released the regulation on rewards for citizens reporting activities that endanger national security who will be given an incentive based on the effectiveness and contribution of their reports, with the maximum amount exceeding 100,000 yuan ($15,000). The MSS article published on Sunday also highlighted several examples of citizens who helped safeguard national security by reporting suspicious activities. They included border residents who stepped forward to confront and thwart suspicious individuals and received awards for particularly significant contributions; a ride-hailing driver who noticed a passenger secretly photographing a sensitive facility and calmly handled the situation; fishermen who retrieved surveillance devices from the sea; and a university student who reported the sale of state secrets. The article said that China's counter-espionage efforts face a severe and complex situation, with foreign intelligence agencies seeking to infiltrate the country and obtain sensitive information. It stressed that safeguarding national security requires not only the efforts of national security authorities but also the participation of the public. The experience of the past 11 years demonstrates that safeguarding national security is a responsibility shared by all, with growing public participation helping strengthen the country's overall national security defenses, it added. Global Times

item.title: US-Japan-ROK coordination plan reflects strategic anxiety, could undermine regional stability under guise of 'stability maintenance': expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01 14:09:00
The G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting convenes in Atlanta, the US on October 31, 2026. Photo: VCG The US is seeking to consolidate its alliance network by linking multiple regional hotspots, including Taiwan island, the South China Sea and the East China Sea, in its trilateral coordination with Japan and South Korea, a move that risks intensifying bloc confrontation and undermining regional stability under the guise of "stability maintenance," a Chinese expert said. The expert's comment came after the three countries' foreign ministers expressed their positions on regional security issues on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta, the US on Friday local time. In a statement, the US State Department claimed the secretary and foreign ministers "emphasized the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Straits." The claims once again reflect Washington's attempt to draw its allies into the Taiwan question and exploit China's internal affairs to serve the US' broader regional strategy, while encouraging the island's authorities to seek external support, rather than contributing to peace and stability across the Taiwan Straits, Zheng Jian, a professor at the Taiwan Research Institute of Xiamen University, told the Global Times on Sunday. A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson has reiterated on multiple occasions that China has an exclusive economic zone and a continental shelf in waters east of Taiwan island. It is fully within China's sovereign rights and jurisdiction, and therefore legitimate, lawful and beyond reproach, for China to carry out activities in these waters. China has never been the party stirring up trouble and disrupting stability in these waters. The notion of "stability" for the US is merely a relative one, which it can interpret and invoke at different stages to justify actions that serve its own interests. This time, Washington is doing so by linking multiple regional flashpoints, making it easier to mobilize its allies in support of its broader "Indo-Pacific" strategy, Zheng said. The emergence of such exclusive groupings in Northeast Asia is also putting regional countries under indirect pressure to take sides, which is detrimental to peace and stability in the region, he added. Alongside this "repeated sensationalism," the US secretary of state and foreign ministers of Japan and South Korea signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) for a Trilateral Arctic Pacific Partnership to explore maritime cooperation and economic partnership in the Pacific Arctic during their meeting on the sidelines. The move reflects Washington's strategic concerns over its limited infrastructure and capabilities in the Arctic, as it seeks to leverage cooperation with Japan and South Korea to strengthen its position in Arctic shipping routes and related areas, Zheng said. Japan's growing involvement may also go beyond economic interests, reflecting its intention to compete with China and Russia in Arctic shipping and related cooperation. However, a MOC and a few working groups cannot conjure up even a single operational heavy icebreaker, highlighting the gap between Washington's strategic ambitions and its actual capabilities in the region, he noted. Zheng added that the broader approach also reflects the Cold War mentality and containment strategy underlying US policy toward China. Japan could meanwhile use Washington's push for greater burden-sharing among allies as an opportunity to expand its military and strategic role in the region, potentially accelerating its remilitarization. Regional countries should therefore assess Washington's moves calmly rather than be swayed by its heightened rhetoric. It's also worth noting that this time, the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting failed to issue a joint communique or reach consensus on key geopolitical and economic security issues, while even the traditional "family photo" session was canceled. Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Ma Zhaoxu called on the G20 to shoulder its due responsibilities amid a turbulent and changing international landscape, serve as a force for safeguarding world peace and stability, help ease tensions and de-escalate regional hotspot issues, address the root causes of conflicts, and strengthen global security governance. China's ability to help resolve issues in the Middle East has demonstrated to the international community its commitment to genuinely pursuing regional peace and stability, which differs fundamentally from the US' notion of "relative stability" that serves primarily its own interests, Zheng said.

item.title: Chinese ship-owner CMES holds vessel-naming ceremony in South Korea, advancing the two countries' shipbuilding cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01 13:53:00
Photo: screenshot of www.imarine.cn The first vessel under China Merchants Energy Shipping's (CMES) second-phase LNG project with QatarEnergy was named in South Korea on October 28-29, according to media reports, marking progress in cooperation between Chinese ship-owners and South Korean shipbuilders. The LEKHRAIB, the first of six 174,000-cubic-meter LNG carriers ordered by CMES from South Korea's Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI), was named during ceremonies held on Geoje Island and in Busan. The vessel will provide long-term LNG transportation services for QatarEnergy. The project forms part of QatarEnergy's fleet expansion to support rising LNG production and exports. In addition to the six vessels built by Samsung Heavy Industries, CMES secured long-term transportation contracts for four larger 271,000-cubic-meter QC MAX carriers, which are being built by China's Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding. LNG carriers are among the most technologically demanding commercial vessels, as they transport natural gas at temperatures of around minus 162 C. Their construction requires specialized cargo containment and insulation systems. The LEKHRAIB features a GTT Mark III Flex membrane containment system, with a designed daily boil-off rate of no more than 0.085 percent, as well as dual-fuel engines. The project reflects the changing dynamics of the global LNG carrier market. South Korean shipbuilders have long held a strong position in large LNG carrier construction, while Chinese shipyards have been expanding their capabilities and securing more orders for advanced vessels, Wang Peng, an associate researcher at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times. The participation of Samsung Heavy Industries and Hudong-Zhonghua in the same project highlights both countries' roles in meeting growing global demand for LNG transportation. Cooperation between Chinese ship-owners and South Korean shipyards is developing alongside competition between the two countries' shipbuilding industries, particularly in the high-end vessel market, Wang said. Global Times

item.title: China-Peru FTA Upgrade Protocol enters into force on Sunday, to boost bilateral economic, trade ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01 12:56:00
Port workers load fresh Peruvian fruit from Chancay Port in Peru, which arrived at Shanghai's Yangshan Port, onto trucks for distribution on December 19, 2024. Photo: VCG The free trade agreement (FTA) Upgrade Protocol between China and Peru entered into force on Sunday, according to a statement seen on China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM). The entry into force and implementation of the protocol will boost China-Peru economic and trade ties, accelerate the two countries’ comprehensive strategic partnership, create a more favorable business environment and trade and investment opportunities for enterprises on both sides, and bring more tangible benefits to the peoples of the two countries, MOFCOM said. Observers expect the protocol to get Peru-produced blueberries, avocados, grapes and fishery products onto Chinese supermarket shelves and dining tables more quickly, while opening a faster lane for Chinese exports of autos and parts, steel, and electronic and telecom equipment to Peru. They also see the Chancay Port – a landmark cooperation project under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) – emerging as a door-to-door hub, with multimodal links and clearer logistics rules helping mineral ores and agri-fishery cargo move more smoothly between the two countries. China and Peru launched FTA upgrade negotiations in November 2018 and signed the Upgrade Protocol on November 14, 2024. Through joint efforts, the two sides recently confirmed that each has completed its respective domestic approval procedures, and the Upgrade Protocol entered into force on Sunday. The protocol upgrades the original agreement by improving seven existing chapters — rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, intellectual property, trade in services, temporary entry of business persons, and investment. It adds five new chapters on standards and conformity assessment cooperation, competition policy, electronic commerce, global supply chains, and environment and trade, according to a report by the China Central Television (CCTV). Among them, the global supply chains chapter — covering such areas as encouraging multimodal transport and promoting foreign-trade logistics corridors and infrastructure — is an innovative step by the two sides under the FTA, underscoring their commitment to jointly safeguarding the stability and smooth flow of supply chains. The standards and conformity assessment cooperation chapter establishes a dedicated cooperation mechanism and sets out a list of intended areas of cooperation, which will provide a platform for mutual recognition of standards and related collaboration between the two countries and help lower trade costs for their enterprises, the MOFCOM statement said. The two sides have also agreed to launch negative-list negotiations on trade in services and investment within two years of the Upgrade Protocol’s entry into force, to further raise openness in these areas between the two countries and continue unlocking the potential of their trade and investment ties. The China-Peru FTA was signed in April 2009 and officially entered into force in March 2010. It was China’s first comprehensive FTA with a Latin American country, and has played a major role in boosting bilateral economic and trade ties. In 2025, bilateral trade volume between China and Peru reached $50.4 billion in 2025, nearly seven times the $6.4 billion recorded in 2009. China and Peru are comprehensive strategic partners with highly complementary economies. China is Peru’s largest trading partner, its largest export market and its largest source of imports, while Peru is China’s fourth-largest trading partner in Latin America and an important investment destination. The Upgrade Protocol also marks a concrete step by China to uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system, and demonstrates China’s resolve to work with other countries through free trade negotiations to safeguard multilateralism and free trade, MOFCOM said. Global Times

item.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles: A blank check to Ukraine, a bill for Europe?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31 16:56:00
US' game of manipulation Illustration: Liu Rui/GT At first glance, the US approval of the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine may look like a long-awaited boost to Ukraine's air defenses. But a closer look reveals a rather different arrangement: Is this another blank check from the US, with the approved deal expected to be financed by US allies despite an unclear delivery timeline? On Friday, the US State Department announced that Washington had approved the proposed sale of 500 Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (PAC-3 MSE) missiles to Ukraine. The deal, which is still subject to congressional review, is valued at approximately $2.1 billion. According to the US government, "no US funds are involved in this sale." Instead, the purchase will be "funded entirely by partners and allies," particularly those in Europe. "Ukraine will pay for this purchase with donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds, financed by the European Union's Ukraine Support Loan," the announcement said. Why approve the sale now? On the one hand, Washington has faced growing questions from European allies about its approach to the conflict, particularly following its engagement with Russia and earlier tensions over intelligence support for Kiev. It appears that approving the sale is intended to send a signal that the US remains committed to supporting Ukraine, while offering some reassurance to increasingly uneasy European partners. On the other hand, as Chinese military expert Song Zhongping told the Global Times, Patriot missiles are defensive weapons and are therefore less likely to provoke a strong reaction from Moscow. In this way, Washington can worry less about escalating tensions with Moscow. Crucially, however, it can do so without committing American taxpayer money to the purchase, while still bringing sound commercial benefits to the US politico-military-industrial complex. Lockheed Martin will be the principal contractor. As Song points out, if other countries are willing to pay and American companies are ready to supply the weapons, why turn down an order worth more than $2 billion? This reflects the current US administration's increasingly transaction-oriented approach to the Ukraine conflict: The US can retain political influence and reap commercial benefits while shifting much of the financial burden onto its allies. But there is a major gap between approving a weapons sale and actually delivering the weapons. According to the BBC, the 500 interceptors have yet to enter production and are not expected to be delivered soon. Production capacity is another constraint, as the US Department of Defense previously reported an annual PAC-3 MSE production capacity of around 600 missiles. Ukraine, meanwhile, needs the interceptors now. Kiev has urged Washington to accelerate deliveries, but the US must also consider its own military requirements and commitments to other allies. The answer for Ukraine is clear: The timing of delivery remains largely in Washington's hands. And even if all 500 Patriot missiles eventually arrive, how much difference will they make on the battlefield? Song argues that the number, while seemingly substantial, is unlikely to be enough to meet Ukraine's needs in the face of sustained Russian attacks. With Russia employing a range of strike capabilities, the interceptors could be used up quickly. The implications for Europe go well beyond the cost of this particular purchase. On the surface, the arrangement looks like a straightforward division of responsibilities within the transatlantic alliance. In reality, it reinforces an increasingly unequal relationship. Washington retains control over the production and supply of critical military equipment, and American defense contractors secure valuable orders. European countries, by contrast, shoulder a growing share of the financial burden while remaining heavily dependent on US weapons and security guarantees. More concerning still, this model risks locking Europe into a costly cycle. As the conflict continues, Ukraine will need more weapons; as those needs grow, European governments will face pressure to commit more funds. Meanwhile, the financial and economic costs of a prolonged conflict continue to accumulate. Europe could find itself carrying an ever-greater share of the burden, and ultimately, it is ordinary EU citizens who have to bear the overall economic consequences. This sale of 500 Patriot missiles offers a snapshot of the unequal distribution of influence, benefits, and costs among the US, Europe and Ukraine regarding the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The US sells, Europe pays, and Ukraine waits. For Kiev, the promised "timely assistance" may arrive far too late. For Europe, the more pressing question is how much longer it will be expected to foot the bill.

item.title: 'Consistency is valuable in governance' – this ancient saying is worth heeding by the German side: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31 01:02:00
Photo:VCG While Germany focuses on issues like market access, supply chain security, and industrial competition, China likewise places great importance on a fair business environment and the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises. What both sides need is to establish more effective communication and coordination mechanisms to identify a new balance of interests in areas such as industrial upgrading, technological innovation, and economic and trade rules. President Xi Jinping held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier at the Great Hall of the People on Friday afternoon. This marks the return to China - after an eight-year hiatus - of Steinmeier, an old friend of the Chinese people. The visit comes at a pivotal juncture, as the two nations approach the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations, and at a critical moment when China-EU economic and trade ties, following multiple rounds of consultations, are seeking a period of relative stability. The two heads of state engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on a range of major issues, including China-Germany relations, China-EU cooperation, and global governance, sending a clear signal in favor of openness over isolation, and cooperation over confrontation. During the talks, President Xi stressed that consistency is valuable in governance. This ancient saying, drawn from the Confucian classic Book of Documents , encapsulates the ancient wisdom of the sages: effective governance requires sustained stability, while frequent, capricious policy shifts are to be avoided. This offers highly relevant insights for today's China-Germany and China-Europe relations, and is worth heeding by the German side. China adopts a forward-looking view of its relations with Germany and the EU, and does not allow temporary frictions to derail the broader trajectory of cooperation. Germany and the European side should work with China in the same direction, and maintain a "consistent" resolve amid changes unseen in a century. This, too, is a test of political wisdom. President Steinmeier noted that he has visited China eight times over the past 25 years, witnessing its rapid development and observing a fresh, evolving landscape with each trip. China's rapid development is truly worth a visit from our German friends who can bring back their fresh impressions to Germany, which will help deepen an accurate understanding between the two nations and open up new possibilities for mutually beneficial cooperation. This year, several core production units at BASF's integrated site in Zhanjiang have come online. As the first stop on his visit, President Steinmeier toured the Volkswagen R&D center in Hefei, East China's Anhui, where he saw firsthand the "intelligent brain" for vehicles - a system developed jointly by Chinese and German teams - and test-drove a new-energy vehicle equipped with advanced autonomous driving technologies. These vivid, concrete outcomes underscore a significant evolution in China-Germany cooperation: a transition from a relationship based on the complementarity of markets and technologies toward one defined by joint innovation. This is not a one-sided dynamic of dependency, but rather the result of market-driven choices and mutually beneficial cooperation. In recent years, there has been a growing sense of "dependency anxiety" regarding China within Germany, alongside an increasing tendency to interpret economic and trade issues through a security lens. While Germany's desire to strengthen its economic resilience is understandable, this objective is not at odds with deepening cooperation with China. The stability of China's policy toward Germany does not imply an absence of diverging interests; rather, it underscores that such differences should be addressed within the context of a long-term strategic relationship. While Germany focuses on issues like market access, supply chain security, and industrial competition, China likewise places great importance on a fair business environment and the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises. What both sides need is to establish more effective communication and coordination mechanisms, through which both sides can identify a new balance of interests in areas such as industrial upgrading, technological innovation, and economic and trade rules. China's continuous opening-up further creates conditions for German companies to participate in this process. The positive signals emanating from the meeting between the Chinese and German leaders inject new momentum into China-Europe relations. While the relationship has weathered various storms, the challenges that have emerged during the course of cooperation are simply issues that arise in the process of development and progress. As the Chinese often say, problems encountered during development should be resolved through further development; similarly, the Germans frequently remark that "life is not a parking lot, but a driving lane." From trade consultations regarding electric vehicles to multiple rounds of dialogue on industrial policy, the twists and turns experienced by China and the EU in recent years have consistently led back to the negotiating table - where, through equal dialogue, solutions addressing the legitimate concerns of both sides have been found. This clearly demonstrates that China and Europe are fully capable of properly handling the contradictions and differences that arise in the course of their development, and of returning to the correct positioning of their partnership. As the "bellwether" of the EU, Germany is well-positioned - and has a responsibility - to play a more active role in fostering rational dialogue between China and the EU, and in upholding open cooperation. Next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Germany. For over half a century, Germany has gained significant development opportunities from China's economic growth. As China's economic structure and industrial capabilities evolve, Germany needs to make corresponding adjustments - starting with an updated understanding of China. If Germany aspires to play a greater role in the Asia-Pacific and in international affairs, it should recognize the value of China and Germany working together toward the same direction. The more turbulent and complex the world becomes, the more steadfast and confident China and Germany should remain in their cooperation. By staying on the right course, solidifying the foundation of mutual trust, and broadening the scope of collaboration - while resisting the pull of unilateralism and ignoring short-term, distracting noise - the two nations can continue to inject more positive energy into their bilateral relationship, China-EU relations, and global governance as a whole.

item.title: Chinese tech firm gives employees gold keyboard keycaps for fifth straight year
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 14:05:00
A tech company in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, gave 20 gold keyboard keycaps to outstanding employees as gifts for Programmers' Day in China on October 24. Photos: Jimu News A tech company in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, gave 20 gold keyboard keycaps to outstanding employees as gifts for Programmers' Day in China on October 24. One of the keycaps, a gold space bar weighing about 35 grams, is worth more than 40,000 yuan ($6,000), Jimu News reported. The company, Insta360, an intelligent imaging technology firm, has presented gold keycaps to outstanding employees for five consecutive years, giving away a total of 75, according to the media report. Nearly 60 percent of its workforce is engaged in research and development (R&D), with R&D personnel playing a key role in driving product innovation. Each year, the largest gold space bar is awarded to the programmer who has made the greatest contribution to the company. This year, the company also introduced gold "F5" keys, symbolizing iterative improvement and innovation. Each F5 key is worth nearly 10,000 yuan, while all the keycaps are made of approximately 99.9 percent pure gold. With gold prices fluctuating, the gold keycaps have unexpectedly become a kind of "investment product" in employees' eyes, although many choose to keep them as souvenirs. In a post on his Sina Weibo account recently, Insta360 CEO Liu Jingkang said that a young colleague had suggested giving this year's gold keycaps to artificial intelligence (AI) instead of employees, but he disagreed. While AI has made it possible to generate code in ever-greater quantities, the value that exceptional people can create has actually become even greater, Liu said. As more code is generated by AI, the company still chooses to reward human creativity with real gold, he added. Global Times

item.title: Merz's flattery of Takaichi was politically frivolous
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 11:12:00
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (R) and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz hold a joint press conference after their talks at the prime minister's office in Tokyo on October 28, 2026. Photo: VCG During his visit to Japan, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that despite the geographical distance between the two countries, calling each other neighbors would not be an overstatement. He also described Germany and Japan as "Premium Partners," emphasizing that the two sides share similar interests and values. While expressing a sense of closeness is not unusual in diplomatic settings, characterizing two countries separated by 9,000 kilometers as "neighbors" - and using "shared values" as a pretext to advance a series of security and economic arrangements with clear, targeted objectives - goes well beyond mere rhetoric. By framing Germany and Japan as "neighbors," Merz is not truly referring to geography, but rather to political alignment. As developed economies, Germany and Japan share common interests in upholding multilateral trade and addressing climate change. However, these interests can be addressed through established bilateral and multilateral channels, without drawing lines based on "shared values." It is worth noting that Germany's postwar reflection on its own history has left a deep impression on nations across Asia. In contrast, since the current Japanese administration took office, there have been clear signs of a distorted view of history and moves toward "remilitarization," prompting neighboring countries to remain vigilant. By emphasizing "shared values" with Japan at this particular moment, how does Merz expect Asian countries to view Germany? In fact, Merz is doing more than just signaling closer ties with Japan; he has explicitly called for stronger military cooperation between the two countries. Germany has also expressed interest in joining the Global Combat Air Program - a joint initiative involving Japan, the UK, and Italy. The fact that two nations defeated in World War II are so eagerly moving to the forefront of military cooperation, while selectively emphasizing "shared values" and deliberately sidestepping the postwar international order's constraints on military activities, is in itself enough to warrant vigilance from the international community. On the Taiwan question, Merz also remarked that Germany will decide how to implement the one-China policy, an attempt to create a "gray area" on a matter of principle. Such attempts to test the boundaries are in no way constructive for China-Germany relations. Merz's flattery toward Takaichi goes beyond mere "cozying up" - it is a clear display of political frivolity. China has never opposed other nations developing normal relations; however, any cooperation implicitly directed against China deviates from the proper course of state-to-state relations. The German business community had generally hoped that Merz's trip to Asia would help secure orders and improve supply-chain links. Yet Merz has clearly failed to demonstrate the rationality expected of a mature political figure during this visit. The Chinese foreign ministry has previously expressed the hope that Germany and the EU will remain objective and rational, work with China in the same direction, and become reliable and predictable partners for each other. Merz would do well to heed this advice. One might attempt to "claim" a neighbor from 9,000 kilometers away, but genuine partnership requires sincerity and mutual respect.

item.title: From anxiety to calm: Chinese support transforms maternal, child healthcare in western Pakistan
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30 08:49:00
This file photo shows medical supplies donated by China at a hospital in Quetta, Pakistan. (Xinhua) For 28-year-old Gul Bano, the birth of her fourth child brought something she had not experienced during her previous three deliveries -- a sense of calm. Two months ago, Bano arrived at a basic health unit in the provincial capital city of Balochistan to give birth. Unlike her earlier experiences, she found herself surrounded by modern medical equipment, trained health workers, and a clean, well-equipped delivery room. "This time, I was not afraid," Bano said, recalling the day her baby was born. "Everything was available here, and the delivery was much easier than it was a few years ago." Among the equipment that assisted her was a vein detector, which makes it easier to locate veins, particularly when an intravenous line or blood sample is needed, as well as a vacuum extractor, making it easier for her to deliver. For Bano, however, the difference was not only about medical equipment. She said the care she received made her feel respected and comfortable. "My husband works as a daily-wage laborer and earns less than 5 U.S. dollars a day, hindering us as a family from affording quality healthcare. Here, everything was provided to me free of charge, even the delivery gown. The bed was clean, and the equipment was ready," she said. "I did not have to worry about anything." Her experience reflects the changes taking place in maternal and child healthcare facilities across Balochistan. Supported by the government of China, these facilities are offering safer and more dignified childbirth services for mothers. China has been helping the government of Balochistan in upgrading maternal and child healthcare facilities, including the improvement of 100 medical facilities across the province. The cooperation aims to strengthen medical infrastructure, provide modern equipment, and improve services for mothers and newborns, particularly in areas where access to quality healthcare has traditionally been difficult. For women like Bano, these improvements are not simply about new machines or renovated rooms, but can mean the difference between approaching childbirth with anxiety and facing it with confidence. "I am very happy with the treatment I received," she said. "I thank China for helping us. My fourth child arrived not only as a new member of the family, but also as a reminder of how better healthcare can change a mother's experience at one of the most important moments of her life." Balochistan has the highest maternal and neonatal mortality rates in Pakistan, largely because 70 percent of the population lives in remote, scattered and hard-to-reach areas, Sana Furqan, a medical practitioner at the Basic Health Unit in the Hudda locality of Quetta, told Xinhua. "For decades, access has been the biggest barrier. This China-supported project is the first large-scale targeted intervention focused entirely on mothers and children at the primary healthcare level, bringing life-saving care to the doorstep of women in remote districts," she said. Talking about the newly equipped healthcare facilities and renovation, Furqan said the Chinese government has supplied equipment like ultrasound machines, delivery beds, baby warmers, incubators, and essential laboratory equipment. "This upgrade is going to bring proximity, preparedness, timeliness and continuity, which is critical to prevent deaths from postpartum hemorrhage, sepsis and birth asphyxia," she said, adding that it will also provide solar solutions, ambulances, as well as training for female staff. "The project would have transformative impacts on the basic healthcare system of Balochistan. In the medium term, we expect a measurable reduction in maternal mortality ratio and neonatal mortality rate, and a sharp decline in preventable complications," she added. Furqan believes the assistance is not seen as charity, but as brotherhood. "The people of Balochistan, especially its mothers, will never forget that when they needed help the most, China stood with them." In a conversation with Xinhua, Provincial Health Minister Bakht Muhammad Kakar said that Pakistan-China cooperation in the health sector is opening a new chapter in people-centered development, turning the friendship between the two countries into tangible benefits for communities. China has one of the most advanced, efficient, and equitable healthcare systems in the world, Kakar said, underlining that despite its own vast population, the country has achieved universal maternal and child health coverage, which is an inspiration for Pakistan. "We want to learn from China's experience in maternal health monitoring, village doctor system, and digital health records," the health minister said.
